name: Y2K digicam
summary: The look of a 2 to 5 megapixel CCD compact: deep focus from a tiny sensor, blown highlights, a hard on-camera flash, over-sharpened edges and clumsy white balance. It is a record of a device and now a deliberate nostalgia.

philosophy.core_thesis: The flaws of a cheap early sensor are the style: they mark a moment in time and read as honest.
design_principles: Emulate a small sensor (1/2.7 in, crop factor about 6) with a real focal length of 5.8mm, which is 35mm in 35mm format, and a deep focus from 0.5m to infinity.
Clip the highlights: set the white point at 100% and let skies and skin go to pure white.
Use the pop-up flash on every indoor shot, with a ratio to ambient of 6:1 and a hard, flat face.
Limit the image to 1600×1200 px (2MP) or 2048×1536 px (3MP), saved as a compressed JPEG at quality 60–75.
Add the sensor faults: chroma noise at ISO 200 and above, purple fringing at high-contrast edges and a slight green or magenta cast.
Sharpen with a coarse radius of 1.5 to 2px at amount 150%, as the camera's own processor did.
anti_patterns: Shallow depth of field and creamy bokeh
Medium or large file sizes with fine detail and smooth gradients
Film grain instead of sensor noise
A carefully composed, evenly lit frame

composition.framing: A 4:3 frame, held at arm's length, with the subject centred and a lot of headroom or a cut-off head.
composition.viewpoint: Arm's length at chest or face height, 1 to 3m; often tilted.
composition.geometry: Casual and unplanned; the horizon tilts and the flash casts a hard shadow on the wall behind.
composition.subject_placement: Centred, because the focus point is in the middle of the screen.

light.quality: Built-in flash or direct sun; small, hard and flat.
light.direction: From the camera axis, which flattens the face and throws a shadow edge behind the subject.
light.colour_temperature: Flash 5500K; auto white balance drifts between 4000K and 6500K
light.time_of_day: Any; often a night out or a bright day

lens_and_camera.focal_length: 5.8mm real (35mm in 35mm format); zoom to 17mm real (105mm)
lens_and_camera.aperture: f/2.8 to f/5.6, with an effective depth of field from 0.5m to infinity
lens_and_camera.focus: Fixed deep focus; autofocus hunts in low light and the macro mode starts at 5cm.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Slightly cool or magenta, over-saturated and over-sharpened, with a coarse sensor noise and clipped highlights.
grade_recipe: Resize to 1600×1200 px, then export as JPEG at quality 65.
Set the white point at 100% with a clip of 2% of the highlights.
Raise saturation by +25% and shift the white balance by +300K cool and +8 magenta.
Add chroma noise of 12% at 2px and luminance noise of 6%.
Sharpen at radius 1.8px, amount 150%, to make halos at edges.
Add purple fringing: shift the blue channel by 1px at high-contrast edges.
colour_and_grade.grain: Chroma and luminance noise, no film grain; JPEG blocks visible at 200%

subject_and_staging.staging: None; the photographer shows the moment to friends on the small LCD at once.
subject_and_staging.direction: Subjects mug for the camera, look at the lens and pose with a peace sign; no art direction.

workflow: Import from a memory card with no raw file.
Use the camera's own sharpening and auto white balance.
Add no edits, or a quick auto-contrast in the bundled software.
Share as a small JPEG of 640×480 px for the web.
post_processing.output: A small, over-sharpened JPEG at 640 to 1600 px on the long side, or a 4×6 in lab print.

emotion.target_response: Nostalgia and ease: the viewer feels a night that was not planned and that everyone remembers.

use_cases: fashion and music campaigns with a nostalgic tone
avoid_when: The brief needs a clean, premium or technical image.
Detail must be legible at a large print size.

modifiers.how: Raise the flash ratio to 10:1, drop the ambient two stops and clip the background to black; keep the small sensor and the hard flash.
Replace the clipped highlights with a rolled shoulder at 92%, use a full-frame sensor at f/2 and add a graded look; keep the digital colour.
